part: Asked along the way · Inbox email, tickets, logos, hosting

entries.title: Shop email inside the Inbox
entries.need: Email to info@, sales@ and support@ had no place in the Inbox.
entries.now: Inbox › Email lists the shop’s mail as conversations: read, reply, forward, add a team note or assign it.
try: Open the email from Arman Hossain.
Press Reply all, write a line and send.

entries.title: Cc, Bcc and conversation threads
entries.need: Replies had no copy fields and long conversations were hard to follow.
entries.now: Every reply has To, Cc and Bcc; older messages fold, and a customer’s answer joins the same conversation.
try: Press “2 earlier messages”, then Reply all.

entries.title: Find email by date and filter
entries.need: A long mailbox had no way to find a day’s mail or narrow the list.
entries.now: Filters for date (one day or a range), address, read, attachments, person, customers and orders; numbered pages with a page size.
try: Open Inbox › Email and press the filter button.
Choose Date › On a date… and pick a day.
Change to 10 a page and go to page 2.

entries.title: Urgent tab on Support tickets
entries.need: Urgent tickets were mixed in with everything else in the list.
entries.now: An Urgent tab lists the open tickets marked Urgent, with its count.

entries.title: Zoom and Google Meet logos
entries.need: Meetings showed plain words for Zoom and Google Meet.
entries.now: Meetings, the meeting form, the super admin’s meetings and Connections show the real Zoom and Google Meet logos.
try: Press New meeting and look at Where.

entries.title: RedX shows its own logo
entries.need: RedX showed two letters in a red square instead of its logo.
entries.now: RedX shows its own logo in Connections, Payouts and delivery settings.

entries.title: A calmer top bar
entries.need: The top bar had Settings, Invoices and Files buttons that crowded the search and were rarely used.
entries.now: Those three buttons are gone; Store settings stays in the account menu, invoices in Orders, files in Settings › Media.
try: Look at the top bar: search, Scan, then View store.

entries.title: A Hosting section in Settings
entries.need: Domains, DNS, email records, security and backups were missing or spread over several pages.
entries.now: Settings › Hosting holds what a web host offers, with an Overview of what needs doing first.
try: Read the To do list and press Open on one.
entries.left: Front end only: the live platform’s DNS servers, CDN and certificate service do the real work.

entries.title: Keep the domain’s DNS at GridCommerce
entries.need: A merchant couldn’t manage the DNS records of their own domain.
entries.now: Point the nameservers here, then add, edit or delete any record; service templates, zone import and export, DNSSEC.
try: Press Add record, choose A, name it shop and give an address.
Press Add for a service and add Google Search Console.

entries.title: Email records: SPF, DKIM and DMARC
entries.need: Shops couldn’t set up email checks, so their mail could land in spam.
entries.now: Pick the mailbox provider; MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC are built, checked and added in one click, with a test email.
try: Set DMARC to Quarantine and save.
Press Add records for me, then Send a test email.

entries.title: Certificates, HTTPS and site protection
entries.need: There were no controls for certificates, HTTPS or blocking attacks.
entries.now: Certificates renew by themselves; HTTPS, HSTS, headers, request limits, blocked countries and IPs, and a store password before launch.

entries.title: Speed settings and a speed test
entries.need: Merchants couldn’t clear the cache or see how fast the store loads.
entries.now: Cache times, clearing the cache, image formats and a speed test of the store home on a 3G phone.

entries.title: Site verification codes and root files
entries.need: Google, Meta and Apple Pay verification had nowhere to go.
entries.now: Paste verification codes (the store’s pages carry them) and add files like ads.txt at the domain’s root.

entries.title: Website backups and bandwidth use
entries.need: Merchants couldn’t back up their website or see how much bandwidth it uses.
entries.now: Back up, download and restore the website and settings, ask to restore a nightly backup, and see bandwidth against the plan.
try: Open Settings › Hosting › Backups and press Back up now.
